question: What chemical element does 'N' stand for in the periodic table?
solution:
The correct answer is__** Nitrogen**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• Nitrogen's symbol is N. Nitrogen is number 7 on the periodic table and has 2 core electrons and 5 valence electrons. 
 
• Nitrogen's electron configuration is 1s2 2s2 2p3. Nitrogen, N, is a colorless, odorless, gaseous element that is about four-fifths of the volume of the atmosphere.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Neptunium is a chemical element with the symbol Np and atomic number 93. A radioactive actinide metal, neptunium is the first transuranic element. Its position in the periodic table is just after uranium, named after the planet Uranus. A neptunium atom has 93 protons and 93 electrons, of which seven are valence electrons. 
 
• Neon (Ne), a chemical element, inert gas of Group 18 (noble gases) of the periodic table, used in electric signs and fluorescent lamps.
 
• Neodymium is a chemical element with the symbol Nd and atomic number 60. It is the fourth member of the lanthanide series.
